newsitem.title: USA: U.S. launches new mission to Europe on Iran.
newsitem.headline: U.S. launches new mission to Europe on Iran.

text.p: The United States has launched a new diplomatic mission to persuade European countries to join in a coordinated policy toward Iran, including imposing tough sanctions, the State Department announced on Monday.
Peter Tarnoff, until recently the department's number three official, is in Europe for consultations with allies on this subject, spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Tarnoff, who stepped down last Friday after four years as undersecretary of state for political affairs, is on a mission "to consult with our European allies on our respective policies towards Iran...(and) to explore with our allies practical steps that the international community can take to change Iran's objectionable behaviour, including its support for terrorism, its pursuit of weapons of mass destruction and its position to the Middle East peace process," Burns said.
Tarnoff was in The Hague on Monday, and then left for Bonn. Tarnoff and his delegation will also visit Paris and London, returning to Washington on Wednesday night.

Until recently the United States and Europe have been at logggerheads over Iran, with Washington taking a strict policy of containment bolstered by tough sanctions and the Europeans pursuing a "constructive dialogue."

But a recent Berlin court verdict in which Iranian leaders were judged to have ordered the murders of three Kurdish dissidents and their interpreter has caused most European governments to withdraw their ambassadors from Tehran and to reconsider their policies.
